doc.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

chapter: New York: Jazztet and sidemen years
title: Fast recording sessions in the early 1960s
summary: Albums were knocked out in three or four hours in one or two takes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: What was recording like then as compared to now?

Well then it was much faster. I mean we would go into the studio here in New York and we’d knock out an album in three, maybe four hours. And that was it, you know. Everything was like one or two takes.
But this was material that you were performing out.

Yeah. Even when we played with guys that we didn’t play with all the time, it was just the same way. At that time it was really incredible. You’d go out and do an album and it was three hours, four hours later you were finished you know. It wasn’t until years later that I went in the studio and did an album that took forever you know — that they took a long time on you know.
